newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Izetbegovic threatens to quit over Brcko dispute.
newsitem.headline: Izetbegovic threatens to quit over Brcko dispute.

text.p: The Moslem chairman of the Bosnian collective presidency has threatened to resign if the disputed town of Brcko is awarded to Serbs by an international arbiter, Sarajevo media reported on Thursday.

Alija Izetbegovic issued the warning in a letter sent recently to major powers amid growing indications that the arbitration verdict will hand Brcko to the Serbs, Bosnian federation television reported.
"If this happens, I will resign and I will withdraw from the function from the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina," Izetbegovic's letter said.

The report came as diplomatic sources in Rome said U.S. arbiter Roberts Owen had decided to assign the strategic town to the Serbs subject to international supervision and guarantees for Moslems and Croats. The decision is to be announced on Friday.

Izetbegovic, chair of the inter-ethnic presidency, said handing Brkco to the Serbs would reward ethnic expulsions conducted by conquering Serb forces and would also violate the principles contained in the Dayton peace agreement.
"I think there is no one who could explain to the Bosnian people that it should calmly endure this final injustice," he wrote.
"With a world that is ready to do this I could not cooperate, and because of my function I must (cooperate). The only way out is to resign and to find someone who could do this (cooperate)."

But the former wartime president of Bosnia, whose government fought a 3-1/2 year war against separatist Serb forces, said no Moslem politician would be willing to accept such a verdict and would also refuse the presidency post.

As a result, he said, there would be political chaos. Although the letter was sent a month ago, government officials apparently decided to leak it on Thursday as the deadline approached for the arbitration verdict.
A spokesman for Izetbegovic, Mirza Hajric, said later that a final decision had yet to be taken and details were still under discussion.
"It's still in play. I think we will know the results in the next couple of hours. It looks better than it looked yesterday," Hajric said.
He confirmed Izetbegovic had threatened to resign, adding that he was concerned that he "would not be able to control the situation" if Serbs were allowed to retain control over Brcko.
Several hundred angry Moslem refugees from Brcko began protesting on Thursday after hearing media reports about the fate of their home town.

The refugees blocked a road at the village of Brka in Moslem-Croat federation territory, some three km (two miles) south-east of Brcko. They vowed to resume their protest on Friday, a Reuters correspondent reported.
The Bosnian Serbs view the narrow Brcko land corridor as a lifeline because it links Serb-controlled territory to the west and east and with neighbouring Serbia.
Serb leaders have threatened to go to war over Brcko. Bosnian Serb forces, backed by the Yugoslav army, captured Brcko early in the 1992-95 war and brutally expelled its Moslem and Croat population.
The Moslem-Croat federation has demanded Brcko be awarded to the federation because Moslems and Croats formed a majority of the town's pre-war population before the conflict.
